nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis of CWO
nodes.procedure: CWO was synthesized using a hydrothermal reaction (details in supplementary text, section 1, and fig. S3). The sharp peaks in x-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns from different batches indicate a highly crystalline structure matching a monoclinic CoWO4 phase and the high reproducibility of the synthesis procedure.
nodes.source_text: We thus synthesized CWO using a hydrothermal reaction (supplementary text, section 1, and fig. S3). The sharp peaks in x-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns from different batches indicate a highly crystalline structure matching a monoclinic CoWO4 phase...

nodes.name: KOH Delamination of CWO
nodes.procedure: The as-synthesized CWO material was dispersed in 0.1 M potassium hydroxide (KOH) aqueous solution and treated for 48 hours to perform WO₄²⁻ → OH⁻ and H₂O anion exchange delamination. This resulted in CWO-del-48 with optimal Co/W ratio and OH⁻/H₂O trapping. The process was studied for effects of cation (Li⁺ to Cs⁺), solvent (H₂O, DMSO, NMP), and pH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD patterns of CWO show sharp peaks matching monoclinic CoWO4 phase; CWO-del shows regular shift in 111 peak indicating defects while retaining bulk monoclinic phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The sharp peaks in x-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns from different batches indicate a highly crystalline structure matching a monoclinic CoWO4 phase ... Powder XRD patterns show a regular shift in the most intense 111 peak (table S7), indicating the generation of defects or strain in the crystal structure...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and STEM images show cube-like shape for CWO transitioning to delaminated flake-like shape for CWO-del-48 with comparable particle size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) images show a shape transition from a cube-like CWO ... to a delaminated, flake-like shape after KOH treatment (figs. S22 and S23).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals missing regular (010) crystal plane in CWO-del-48 indicative of defects from WO4^2- leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images reveal the missing regular (010) crystal plane in CWO-del-48 (figs. S22 and S25), indicative of defects arising from WO4^2- leaching.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ Raman shows bathochromic shift (~5-10 cm^-1) for Co-O (~690 cm^-1) and W-O (~886 cm^-1) peaks with increasing delamination time; intensity ratio Co-O/W-O increases up to 48 hours.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ex situ Raman spectroscopy measurements ... reveal a bathochromic shift (~5 to 10 cm^-1) for both Co-O (~690 cm^-1) and W-O (~886 cm^-1) peaks with increasing delamination time (Fig. 2A).

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA-MS revealed ~16% weight loss for CWO-del-48 over 166° to 396°C range due to water and/or OH⁻ ions (four distinct peaks), negligible for CWO and Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric analysis coupled with mass spectroscopy (TGA-MS) revealed an ~16% weight loss for CWO-del-48 over a 166° to 396°C range due to water and/or OH⁻ ions, which is negligible for CWO and Co₃O₄ (Fig. 2B and fig. S39). Four distinct peaks in this range suggest the presence of different water coordination environments (42).

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS of CWO shows OM (528.55 eV) and OL (530.33 eV); CWO-del-48 shows additional OOH (531.6 eV) and OH2O (533.1 eV) peaks with blue shift of OM and OL peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The O 1s peak of nondelaminated samples deconvolutes into two peaks at 528.55 and 530.33 eV, which correspond to metal oxygen (OM) and lattice oxygen (OL) ... CWO-del-48 spectra ... require deconvolution into two additional peaks corresponding to hydroxide (OOH), at 531.6 eV and water species (OH2O, at 533.1 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms increasing W leaching over delamination time with negligible change in Co concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) measurements confirm increasing W leaching over time but negligible change in Co concentration (fig. S35 and table S9).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM EDX mapping shows uniform distribution of Co and W throughout pristine and delaminated nanocrystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Highannular angle dark-field STEM (HAADF-STEM) images, and respective energy-dispersive xray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping of Co and W, show the uniform distribution of Co and W throughout the pristine and delaminated nanocrystals (figs. S26 and S27).

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS spectra indicate reduction in Co/W atomic ratio after delamination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) spectra indicate a reduction in the Co/W atomic ratio after delamination (fig.S28).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM reveals missing planes and corresponding defects in CWO-del-48.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, atomic force microscopy (AFM) reveals missing planes and corresponding defects in CWO-del-48 (figs. S29 to S31), in agreement with HRTEM and STEM results.

nodes.characterization_summary: iDPC-STEM shows regular atomic arrangement of Co, W, O in CWO; CWO-del-48 reveals substantial vacancies due to WO4^2- leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CWO samples exhibit a regular atomic arrangement of Co, W, and O atoms, consistent with a monoclinic phase. CWO-del-48, on the other hand, reveals a substantial number of vacancies due to WO4^2- leaching (fig.S33).

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR reveals HO-H stretching and H-O-H bending vibrational modes with increasing intensity upon delamination, suggesting higher density of trapped water and hydroxide groups.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) measurements ... reveal HO-H stretching and H-O-H bending vibrational modes with increasing intensity upon delamination, suggesting a higher density of trapped and bridged water and hydroxide groups within the crystals (fig. S40).
